findings.title: zero_grad() called after backward() and before step() — weights never update
findings.quote:
losses.backward()
if max_norm > 0:
    torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(model.parameters(), max_norm)
optimizer.zero_grad()
optimizer.step()
findings.claim: In the training loop (train_one_epoch, called from main.py:377) gradients are computed by losses.backward(), then optimizer.zero_grad() wipes them, and only then optimizer.step() runs — so step() always sees zeroed/None gradients.
findings.concern: No parameter is ever updated during training; the 'trained' model is the random initialization, so none of the encoding-accuracy numbers (Tables 1-6) can be produced by this code.
findings.resolution: Move optimizer.zero_grad() to before losses.backward() (standard order: zero_grad → backward → clip → step). See _audit_code/check_optimizer_order.py: repo order gives max param change 0.0, correct order lowers the loss.

findings.title: SetCriterion references undefined lh_rois/rh_rois for per-category readout modes
findings.claim: In SetCriterion.forward, the names lh_rois and rh_rois are never assigned in the function (or module) scope; this branch runs when readout_res is one of visuals/bodies/faces/places/words.
findings.concern: Those readout modes would raise NameError at loss time; it does not affect the headline results, which use readout_res='streams_inc'/'rois_all' (line 193 skips this branch).
findings.resolution: Define the masks (likely self.lh_challenge_rois / self.rh_challenge_rois) or remove the dead branch; confirm whether the per-category readout modes were ever run.

findings.title: Default transformer decoder uses a query-independent global token pool, not cross-attention
findings.claim: The decoder layer used for encoder_arch='transformer' (the default; the arch loaded for every 'Transformer' row in the notebooks) has no attention. It runs the image tokens through a Conv1d token_mixer (defined __init__ lines 292-297) then mean-pools over ALL tokens (.mean(dim=-1)) into one vector that is added identically to every ROI query (memory.unsqueeze(0) broadcast over the query dim).
findings.concern: Every ROI query receives the same global image summary (verified cross-query std ~3e-8, no per-query routing), so the paper's central mechanism — content-based, ROI-specific routing via scaled-dot-product cross-attention (Fig. 1B, §3.2) — is not implemented, and the interpretable per-ROI attention maps (Fig. 5) and attention category-selectivity (Tables 7-10) cannot be produced; the genuine cross-attention lives only in the unused models/custom_transformer.py (CrossAttention).
findings.resolution: Confirm which decoder produced the reported Transformer results; if it is models/transformer.py, the attention-routing and interpretability claims are unsupported. activations.py:30 also hooks decoder.layers[-i].multihead_attn, which this layer does not have.

findings.title: backbone.py imports models.resnet, but models/resnet.py is absent
findings.claim: models/backbone.py unconditionally imports resnet_model from models.resnet at module top level, and is used at line 59 for any 'resnet' backbone, but no models/resnet.py exists anywhere in the repo (verified by directory listing).
findings.concern: The ResNet50 backbone (Table 3) cannot be built, and because the import is top-level, importing models.backbone (reached via main.py → models.brain_encoder) raises ModuleNotFoundError, blocking the entrypoint for every backbone as shipped.
findings.resolution: Add models/resnet.py (the resnet_model wrapper) to the repo, or guard the import. (Possibly an incomplete-clone artifact — the DINOv2 results imply the authors had this file locally; please confirm.)

findings.title: No code for attention category-selectivity (Tables 7-10), BERT text modality (Table 6), or DeepGaze saliency baseline
findings.quote:
To quantify the category selectivity of attention maps, we classified each pixel of the test set images using
YOLOv5 [22] and YOLOv8-face [11] into five categories
findings.claim: The repo contains no script that runs YOLOv5/YOLOv8-face pixel classification for Tables 7-10, no BERT/BLIP captioning backbone for the Table 6 text-modality result (main.py --backbone_arch has no bert/blip option), and no DeepGaze saliency-map baseline for the 'Saliency based integration' rows (Tables 1, 5); grep over all .py finds none of these.
findings.concern: These reported results (Tables 6-10 and the saliency baseline) are not reproducible from the released code; Tables 7-10 additionally require the attention maps that the released decoder cannot produce (see decoder-no-cross-attention).
findings.resolution: Release the YOLO-based selectivity analysis, the BLIP/BERT captioning + text-backbone code, and the DeepGaze saliency baseline, or state they are out of scope for the repo.

findings.title: Paper says 10-fold cross-validation; code does repeated random 90/10 splits
findings.claim: fetch_dataloaders takes 90% of the training images as train and 10% as validation (num_train at line 229) after an unseeded np.random.shuffle that is redone on every run; 'folds' are separate runs re-randomised each time, and their test predictions are ensembled elsewhere.
findings.concern: This is repeated random subsampling (Monte-Carlo CV), not the 10-fold cross-validation stated in §4 — folds are not disjoint and each sample is not held out exactly once — though the held-out test set is separate so the procedure is not invalid, only mis-described.
findings.resolution: Either implement KFold over the training indices, or describe the procedure as repeated random 90/10 splits with prediction averaging across runs.
findings.paper_ref: §4 'we did 10-fold cross validation using the training set'
